newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan smelters to trim output in 2nd half 1996/97.
newsitem.headline: Japan smelters to trim output in 2nd half 1996/97.

text.p: Japan's eight major non-ferrous metal refining companies plan to trim their total output of refined copper and zinc in the half-year to March 1997 from the same year-ago period, according to semi-annual production schedules released over the past week by the individual firms.

The refiners planned a modest 1.1 percent decline in total refined copper output and a 9.0 percent cut in zinc output from actual production in the October-March 1996 period, while lead was slated to rise 4.0 percent.
The lower copper and zinc levels mostly reflect cuts by Mitsubishi Materials Corp.

Mitsubishi shut its Akita zinc refinery earlier this year under a restructuring plan, while copper output was forecast to edge lower due to scheduled maintenance at the Naoshima smelter from mid-March through mid-April 1997.

The eight companies are: Mitsubishi Materials Corp, Nippon Mining and Metals Co, Mitsui Mining and Smelting Co, Sumitomo Metal Mining Co, Furukawa Co, Dowa Mining Co, Toho Zinc Co and Nittetsu Mining Co.

The totals listed below exceed actual Japanese output due to double counting, as each company's data includes both production they toll for other companies and production other companies toll for them.

Industry sources and analysts said tolling amounts for copper were thought to be under 10 percent and little changed from the prior year, although tolling levels were probably higher for lead and zinc.
